design.name: 火鼍
design.brief: The tuo dragon (鼍龙) of the Black River in Journey to the West, reborn as a giant Chinese alligator (扬子鳄) that lives in the rivers of lava: a huge heavy alligator about 6 m long and 1.4 m tall with real crocodilian anatomy — broad blunt snout lined with jagged teeth, small eyes and nostrils high on the head, short sprawling legs with clawed feet, a long heavy tail with a double crest of plates. Its back is armoured with rows of big thick plates of cooled black basalt crust (like solidified lava rock), separated by glowing molten lava seams; a bright molten seam runs along its spine (weak spot). Its belly and the sides of the head are dark red-brown hide. Ancient, heavy and patient.
design.style_note: Stylization: cartoon game proportions in the same family as the desert and frost rosters (jerboa soldier, fire rat, sancai tomb beast, golden snub-nosed monkey): chunky simplified masses, oversized heads and hands or paws, toy-like readable forms with clean bevelled edges. Iron, basalt and bronze as a few big faceted plates with sparse painted wear; lava and fire painted as OPAQUE glowing cracks, seams and solid sculpted flame shapes (never transparent fire, smoke or particles); fur, hair and feathers as a few large carved clumps. Its defence is part of its own body: it holds NO shield and NO weapon.
design.turnaround_pose: standing on all four short sprawling legs like a real alligator in a high walk, body level and lifted just clear of the ground, the four legs planted with front and hind legs clearly separated; head level facing straight ahead with the mouth closed and the teeth showing along the jaw line; the long heavy tail extending straight backwards and resting slightly down; all basalt plates intact, the spine seam and plate seams painted as opaque glowing orange lines (no lava drips, no flames, no halo)
design.turnaround_digits: each front foot with five separate clawed toes and each hind foot with four separate clawed toes; the snout and the whole tail fully inside the frame; in the side views the very long body and tail must fit inside the view with margin (draw it smaller rather than cut it off).
